newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares rise as market eyes SPIF Cesky.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares rise as market eyes SPIF Cesky.

text.p: Czech shares continued to move higher on Thursday with the PX50 index posting its sixth straight rise and its 15th gain in 16 sessions.
The PX50 closed up 0.6 percent to 521.1 while the RPIX index of continuously traded shares rose by nearly one percent to 1,074.7.
All the major issues rose with power utility CEZ the biggest gainer, up 18 crowns, or 1.9 percent, to 989.
Attention again focused on SPIF Cesky closed investment fund, which is managed by SIS, the investment arm of savings bank Ceska Sporitelna.
SPIF rose 22 crowns to a new 12-month high of 420, accounting for well over half the turnover on continuous trading.

The fund began its spectacular uptrend at the beginning of November, when it was below 300 crowns per share, as rumours circulated that SPIF was looking for a way to become an open ended fund, an intention that was confirmed by SIS last week.
"We are looking for a way to become an open ended fund," Pavel Andres of SIS told Reuters.
Since the beginning of November the discount between net assset value per share and SPIF's current price has fallen from over 40 percent to around 30 percent.
Analysts said the issue would probably continue to rise but acknowledged that it was a high risk high reward stock.

"Still there is a good upside at this point, like close to 30 percent, so the investors have to weigh the possible appreciation potential against the risk they are taking," said Jiri Susicky of Patria Finance investment bank.
The key element of risk concerns the possibility of SPIF actually being able to convert itself into an open ended fund.

Legislation is not yet in place to allow for the conversion of closed end funds to open ended funds and SPIF would be relying on an amendement to the investment fund law or a special ruling from the finance ministry.
Susicky said the conversion of SPIF to a holding company could also allow shareholders to realise net asset value but added that he did not know how likely this was to happen.
